proxy_language: Proto-Numic (Northern Uto-Aztecan, Great Basin branch), supplemented by Proto-Sahaptian and Proto-Plateau Penutian for the Columbia Plateau
proxy_rationale: The Western Stemmed Tradition (c. 13,000-8,000 cal BP, possibly pre-Clovis in places like Cooper's Ferry) has no linguistic attestation. Languages of the region (Numic, Sahaptian, Klamath-Modoc, Washo, Kutenai) are recent and Numic spread only ~1,000 years ago, so there is no demonstrable continuity. Proto-Numic (Miller, Lamb, Fowler, Sapir, Charney reconstructions) is used as a defensible regional proxy for the Great Basin core, with Sahaptian for the Plateau flavour. Treat as a stylistic proxy, not a claim of descent.
phonology: Proto-Numic consonants: *p *t *c(ts) *k *kw (plain and geminate/fortis vs lenis contrast), *s, *h, *m *n *ng, *w *y; some reconstructions add *z-like lenis fricatives. Vowels: *i *a *u *e(=schwa-like i/ɨ) *o; length contrast in Numic daughters. Sahaptian adds ejectives (p' t' k' q'), uvulars (q x), labialised velars/uvulars, lateral fricatives, and a rich cluster system. No tone; stress-accent weak and predictable.
phonotactics: Proto-Numic: syllables (C)V(C); roots mostly CVCV or CVCCV; CC clusters only across syllable boundaries (often nasal+stop, geminates, or h+C preaspirated stops); no word-initial clusters; words traditionally end in vowels in nouns because of final-vowel (absolutive) suffixes, e.g. -pa/-ci/-tu. Western Numic and Central Numic often have final-vowel devoicing, not shown in orthography. Sahaptian words allow heavier clusters but a name builder should keep these rare.
orthography: Use Americanist-style Latin transliteration as in Numic dictionaries (Miller, Sapir's Southern Paiute, Lamb): p t c(ts) k kw s h m n ng w y, vowels a e i o u, with u/o and i/e varying by dialect; long vowels as doubled letters (aa, ii, uu); glottal stop as an apostrophe. Keep ng as a digraph. Avoid c as /k/; c = ts per Numic convention.
morphology: Agglutinative, suffixing, SOV, postpositional. Nouns: root + absolutive suffix (-pa, -ci, -tu, -ka, -wi, -ni, depending on class) that drops under compounding or possession; plural/dual suffixes; possessive prefixes (ni-, i-, ma- 'my, this, that'). Verbs: root + aspect/tense suffixes (-ka durative, -ti/-tu 'make', -wi; nominalisers -pi, -tu 'one who', -nta 'instrument/agent'). Reduplication marks plurals and distributives (CV- copy of first syllable). Sahaptian by contrast is prefix- and suffix-heavy with ergative case, but a name builder should use the Numic frame.
compounding: Head-final: modifier + head, with the modifier stripped of its absolutive suffix, e.g. *pa- 'water' + *tosa 'white' giving a compound of the type water+white. 'X of Y' is Y + X by juxtaposition or with the genitive -n/-na on the possessor (Numic -ni/-n possessive). Agent names: object + verb + agentive (-tu/-nta), e.g. seed-grind-er. Place names: noun + locative -pa/-pa 'at, place of' or -ngwa; plant/animal+locative is typical ('X-place').
noun_phrase_order: Modifier (adjective, possessor, demonstrative) precedes head noun; numerals precede; relative clauses are nominalised and pre-head. Word order within name phrases: [Possessor-n] [Modifier] [Head].
